verses.original: Καὶ εἶδον οὐρανὸν καινὸν καὶ γῆν καινήν ὁ γὰρ πρῶτος οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ πρώτη γῆ ἀπῆλθαν καὶ ἡ θάλασσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἔτι
verses.transliteration: Kai eidon ouranon kainon kai gēn kainēn ho gar prōtos ouranos kai hē prōtē gē apēlthan kai hē thalassa ouk estin eti
verses.literal: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth for the first heaven and - earth had passed away and the sea was no more
verses.literalPt: Vi um novo céu e uma nova terra, porque o primeiro céu e a primeira terra já se foram, e o mar já não é.

verses.original: καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινὴν εἶδον καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡτοιμασμένην ὡς νύμφην κεκοσμημένην τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: kai tēn polin tēn hagian Ierousalēm kainēn eidon katabainousan ek tou ouranou apo tou Theou hētoimasmenēn hōs nymphēn kekosmēmenēn tō andri autēs
verses.literal: I saw the holy city the new Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God prepared as a bride adorned for her husband
verses.literalPt: Vi também a Cidade Santa, a nova Jerusalém, descendo do céu, da parte de Deus, preparada como uma noiva adornada para seu noivo.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου λεγούσης Ἰδοὺ ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ σκηνώσει μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ αὐτοὶ λαοὶ αὐτοῦ ἔσονται καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔσται αὐτῶν θεός
verses.transliteration: Kai ēkousa phōnēs megalēs ek tou thronou legousēs Idou hē skēnē tou Theou meta tōn anthrōpōn kai skēnōsei met’ autōn kai autoi laoi autou esontai kai autos ho Theos met’ autōn estai autōn theos
verses.literal: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying Behold the dwelling place of God is with man and He will dwell with them They will be His people and God Himself will be with them as their God
verses.literalPt: Ouvi uma grande voz, vinda do trono, dizendo: Eis o tabernáculo de Deus está com os homens, e ele habitará com eles; eles serão o seu povo, e Deus mesmo estará com eles.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξαλείψει πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν καὶ ὁ θάνατος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι οὔτε πένθος οὔτε κραυγὴ οὔτε πόνος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι ὅτι τὰ πρῶτα ἀπῆλθαν
verses.transliteration: kai exaleipsei pan dakryon ek tōn ophthalmōn autōn kai ho thanatos ouk estai eti oute penthos oute kraugē oute ponos ouk estai eti hoti ta prōta apēlthan
verses.literal: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain - for the former things have passed away
verses.literalPt: e enxugará toda lágrima dos olhos deles. Não haverá mais morte, nem haverá mais pranto, nem choro, nem dor, porque as primeiras coisas são passadas.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ Ἰδοὺ καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα καὶ λέγει Γράψον ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί εἰσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen ho kathēmenos epi tō thronō Idou kaina poiō panta kai legei Grapson hoti houtoi hoi logoi pistoi kai alēthinoi eisin
verses.literal: And the One seated on the throne said Behold I make all things new Then He said Write this down for these words are faithful and true
verses.literalPt: Disse aquele que estava sentado sobre o trono: Eis que faço novas todas as coisas. Disse-me ele também: Escreve, porque estas palavras são fiéis e verdadeiras.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπέν μοι Γέγοναν ἐγὼ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος ἐγὼ τῷ διψῶντι δώσω ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς τοῦ ὕδατος τῆς ζωῆς δωρεάν
verses.transliteration: kai eipen moi Gegonan egō eimi to Alpha kai to Ō hē archē kai to telos egō tō dipsōnti dōsō ek tēs pēgēs tou hydatos tēs zōēs dōrean
verses.literal: And He told me It is done I am the Alpha and the Omega the Beginning and the End To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life
verses.literalPt: Disse-me ainda: Tudo está cumprido. Eu sou o Alfa e o Ômega, o Princípio e o Fim. Àquele que tem sede, eu lhe darei a beber gratuitamente da fonte da água da vida.

verses.original: ὁ νικῶν κληρονομήσει ταῦτα καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ Θεὸς καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι υἱός
verses.transliteration: ho nikōn klēronomēsei tauta kai esomai autō Theos kai autos estai moi huios
verses.literal: The one who overcomes will inherit all things and I will be his God and he will be My son
verses.literalPt: O vencedor herdará essas coisas; eu serei o seu Deus, e ele será meu filho.

verses.original: Τοῖς δὲ δειλοῖς καὶ ἀπίστοις καὶ ἐβδελυγμένοις καὶ φονεῦσιν καὶ πόρνοις καὶ φαρμάκοις καὶ εἰδωλολάτραις καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ψευδέσιν τὸ μέρος αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ τῇ καιομένῃ πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ ὅ ἐστιν ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος
verses.transliteration: Tois de deilois kai apistois kai ebdelygmenois kai phoneusin kai pornois kai pharmakois kai eidōlolatrais kai pasin tois pseudesin to meros autōn en tē limnē tē kaiomenē pyri kai theiō ho estin ho thanatos ho deuteros
verses.literal: But to the cowardly and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur This is the second death
verses.literalPt: Mas, quanto aos medrosos, e aos incrédulos, e aos abomináveis, e aos homicidas, e aos fornicários, e aos feiticeiros, e aos idólatras, e a todos os mentirosos, sua parte será no lago que arde com fogo e enxofre, que é a segunda morte.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τῶν γεμόντων τῶν ἑπτὰ πληγῶν τῶν ἐσχάτων καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετ’ ἐμοῦ λέγων Δεῦρο δείξω σοι τὴν νύμφην τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀρνίου
verses.transliteration: Kai ēlthen heis ek tōn hepta angelōn tōn echontōn tas hepta phialas tōn gemontōn tōn hepta plēgōn tōn eschatōn kai elalēsen met’ emou legōn Deuro deixō soi tēn nymphēn tēn gynaika tou arniou
verses.literal: Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls full of the seven final plagues came and said to me Come I will show you the bride the wife of the Lamb
verses.literalPt: Veio um dos sete anjos que tinham as sete taças cheias das sete últimas pragas e falou comigo: Vem cá, e mostrar-te-ei a noiva, a esposa do Cordeiro.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με ἐν Πνεύματι ἐπὶ ὄρος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai apēnenken me en Pneumati epi oros mega kai hypsēlon kai edeixen moi tēn polin tēn hagian Ierousalēm katabainousan ek tou ouranou apo tou Theou
verses.literal: And he carried me away . . . in the Spirit to a mountain great and high and showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God
verses.literalPt: Levou-me, pelo Espírito, a um grande e alto monte e mostrou-me a Santa Cidade de Jerusalém, descendo do céu, da parte de Deus,

verses.original: ἔχουσαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ φωστὴρ αὐτῆς ὅμοιος λίθῳ τιμιωτάτῳ ὡς λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι κρυσταλλίζοντι
verses.transliteration: echousan tēn doxan tou Theou ho phōstēr autēs homoios lithō timiōtatō hōs lithō iaspidi krystallizonti
verses.literal: shining with the glory of God Its radiance was like a most precious jewel like a jasper . . . as clear as crystal
verses.literalPt: e tendo a glória de Deus. O seu brilho era semelhante a uma pedra preciosíssima, como pedra de jaspe cristalina.

verses.original: ἔχουσα τεῖχος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν ἔχουσα πυλῶνας δώδεκα καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν ἀγγέλους δώδεκα καὶ ὀνόματα ἐπιγεγραμμένα ἅ ἐστιν τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα φυλῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ
verses.transliteration: echousa teichos mega kai hypsēlon echousa pylōnas dōdeka kai epi tois pylōsin angelous dōdeka kai onomata epigegrammena ha estin ta onomata tōn dōdeka phylōn huiōn Israēl
verses.literal: The city had a great and high wall with twelve gates inscribed - with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel and twelve angels at the gates
verses.literalPt: Tinha um muro grande e alto. Tinha doze portas, e, junto às portas, doze anjos, e, sobre elas, nomes escritos, que são os da doze tribos dos filhos de Israel.

verses.original: ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς πυλῶνες τρεῖς καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ πυλῶνες τρεῖς καὶ ἀπὸ νότου πυλῶνες τρεῖς καὶ ἀπὸ δυσμῶν πυλῶνες τρεῖς
verses.transliteration: apo anatolēs pylōnes treis kai apo borra pylōnes treis kai apo notou pylōnes treis kai apo dysmōn pylōnes treis
verses.literal: There were three gates on the east three on the north three on the south and three on the west
verses.literalPt: Três portas estavam ao oriente; três portas, ao norte; três portas, ao sul; e três portas, ao ocidente.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ τεῖχος τῆς πόλεως ἔχων θεμελίους δώδεκα καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ Ἀρνίου
verses.transliteration: kai to teichos tēs poleōs echōn themelious dōdeka kai ep’ autōn dōdeka onomata tōn dōdeka apostolōn tou Arniou
verses.literal: The wall of the city had twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb
verses.literalPt: O muro da cidade tinha doze fundamentos e sobre estes os doze nomes dos doze apóstolos do Cordeiro.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶχεν μέτρον κάλαμον χρυσοῦν ἵνα μετρήσῃ τὴν πόλιν καὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai ho lalōn met’ emou eichen metron kalamon chrysoun hina metrēsē tēn polin kai tous pylōnas autēs kai to teichos autēs
verses.literal: The angel who spoke with me had a golden measuring rod to measure the city and its gates and - walls
verses.literalPt: O que falava comigo tinha uma cana de ouro, que servia de medida, para medir a cidade, as suas portas e o seu muro.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ πόλις τετράγωνος κεῖται καὶ τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς ὅσον καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὴν πόλιν τῷ καλάμῳ ἐπὶ σταδίων δώδεκα χιλιάδων τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ τὸ ὕψος αὐτῆς ἴσα ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: kai hē polis tetragōnos keitai kai to mēkos autēs hoson kai to platos kai emetrēsen tēn polin tō kalamō epi stadiōn dōdeka chiliadōn to mēkos kai to platos kai to hypsos autēs isa estin
verses.literal: The city lies foursquare with its width the same as its length And he measured the city with the rod and all its dimensions were equal 12,000 . . . stadia in length and width and height
verses.literalPt: A cidade é quadrangular, de comprimento igual à largura. Ele mediu a cidade com a cana, e tinha doze mil estádios; o seu comprimento, e a sua largura, e a sua altura são iguais.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τεσσάρων πηχῶν μέτρον ἀνθρώπου ὅ ἐστιν ἀγγέλου
verses.transliteration: kai emetrēsen to teichos autēs hekaton tesserakonta tessarōn pēchōn metron anthrōpou ho estin angelou
verses.literal: And he measured its wall to be 144 . . . . . . cubits by the human measure the angel was using
verses.literalPt: Mediu também o seu muro, e ele tinha cento e quarenta e quatro cúbitos, segundo a medida de homem, isto é, de anjo.

verses.original: Καὶ ἡ ἐνδώμησις τοῦ τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις καὶ ἡ πόλις χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὅμοιον ὑάλῳ καθαρῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai hē endōmēsis tou teichous autēs iaspis kai hē polis chrysion katharon homoion hyalō katharō
verses.literal: The wall was made of jasper and the city itself of pure gold as pure as glass
verses.literalPt: O muro era construído de jaspe, e a cidade era de ouro semelhante a vidro puro.

verses.original: οἱ θεμέλιοι τοῦ τείχους τῆς πόλεως παντὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ κεκοσμημένοι ὁ θεμέλιος ὁ πρῶτος ἴασπις ὁ δεύτερος σάπφιρος ὁ τρίτος χαλκηδών ὁ τέταρτος σμάραγδος
verses.transliteration: hoi themelioi tou teichous tēs poleōs panti lithō timiō kekosmēmenoi ho themelios ho prōtos iaspis ho deuteros sapphiros ho tritos chalkēdōn ho tetartos smaragdos
verses.literal: The foundations of the city walls were adorned with every kind of precious stone The first foundation was jasper the second sapphire the third chalcedony the fourth emerald
verses.literalPt: Os fundamentos do muro da cidade eram adornados com toda espécie de pedras preciosas. O primeiro fundamento era de jaspe; o segundo, de safira; o terceiro, de calcedônia; o quarto, de esmeralda;

verses.original: ὁ πέμπτος σαρδόνυξ ὁ ἕκτος σάρδιον ὁ ἕβδομος χρυσόλιθος ὁ ὄγδοος βήρυλλος ὁ ἔνατος τοπάζιον ὁ δέκατος χρυσόπρασος ὁ ἑνδέκατος ὑάκινθος ὁ δωδέκατος ἀμέθυστος
verses.transliteration: ho pemptos sardonyx ho hektos sardion ho hebdomos chrysolithos ho ogdoos bēryllos ho enatos topazion ho dekatos chrysoprasos ho hendekatos hyakinthos ho dōdekatos amethystos
verses.literal: the fifth sardonyx the sixth carnelian the seventh chrysolite the eighth beryl the ninth topaz the tenth chrysoprase the eleventh jacinth and the twelfth amethyst
verses.literalPt: o quinto, de sardônio; o sexto, de sárdio; o sétimo, de crisólito; o oitavo, de berilo; o nono, de topázio; o décimo, de crisópraso; o undécimo, de jacinto; e o duodécimo, de ametista.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ δώδεκα πυλῶνες δώδεκα μαργαρῖται ἀνὰ εἷς ἕκαστος τῶν πυλώνων ἦν ἐξ ἑνὸς μαργαρίτου καὶ ἡ πλατεῖα τῆς πόλεως χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὡς ὕαλος διαυγής
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi dōdeka pylōnes dōdeka margaritai ana heis hekastos tōn pylōnōn ēn ex henos margaritou kai hē plateia tēs poleōs chrysion katharon hōs hyalos diaugēs
verses.literal: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls with each - gate consisting of a single pearl The main street of the city was pure gold as clear as glass
verses.literalPt: As doze portas eram doze pérolas; e cada uma das portas era feita de uma só pérola. A rua da cidade era de ouro puro como vidro transparente.

verses.original: Καὶ ναὸν οὐκ εἶδον ἐν αὐτῇ ὁ γὰρ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὁ Παντοκράτωρ ναὸς αὐτῆς ἐστιν καὶ τὸ Ἀρνίον
verses.transliteration: Kai naon ouk eidon en autē ho gar Kyrios ho Theos ho Pantokratōr naos autēs estin kai to Arnion
verses.literal: But I saw no temple in the city because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple
verses.literalPt: Não vi nela santuário, porque o Senhor Deus Todo-Poderoso, e o Cordeiro são o seu santuário.

verses.original: καὶ ἡ πόλις οὐ χρείαν ἔχει τοῦ ἡλίου οὐδὲ τῆς σελήνης ἵνα φαίνωσιν αὐτῇ ἡ γὰρ δόξα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐφώτισεν αὐτήν καὶ ὁ λύχνος αὐτῆς τὸ Ἀρνίον
verses.transliteration: kai hē polis ou chreian echei tou hēliou oude tēs selēnēs hina phainōsin autē hē gar doxa tou Theou ephōtisen autēn kai ho lychnos autēs to Arnion
verses.literal: And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it because the glory of God illuminates the city and the Lamb is its lamp
verses.literalPt: A cidade não precisa do sol nem da lua para a iluminar; porque a glória de Deus a iluminou, e o Cordeiro é a sua candeia.

verses.original: καὶ περιπατήσουσιν τὰ ἔθνη διὰ τοῦ φωτὸς αὐτῆς καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς φέρουσιν τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν εἰς αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: kai peripatēsousin ta ethnē dia tou phōtos autēs kai hoi basileis tēs gēs pherousin tēn doxan autōn eis autēn
verses.literal: By its light the nations will walk and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory
verses.literalPt: As nações caminharão à sua luz, e os reis da terra lhe trarão a sua glória.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ πυλῶνες αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν ἡμέρας νὺξ γὰρ οὐκ ἔσται ἐκεῖ
verses.transliteration: kai hoi pylōnes autēs ou mē kleisthōsin hēmeras nyx gar ouk estai ekei
verses.literal: Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day because there will be no night there
verses.literalPt: As suas portas não se fecharão de dia, porque noite não haverá ali.

verses.original: Καὶ οἴσουσιν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: Kai oisousin tēn doxan kai tēn timēn tōn ethnōn eis autēn
verses.literal: And into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations
verses.literalPt: A ela trarão a glória e a honra das nações.

verses.original: καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτὴν πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ὁ ποιῶν βδέλυγμα καὶ ψεῦδος εἰ μὴ οἱ γεγραμμένοι ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ Ἀρνίου
verses.transliteration: kai ou mē eiselthē eis autēn pan koinon kai ho poiōn bdelygma kai pseudos ei mē hoi gegrammenoi en tō bibliō tēs zōēs tou Arniou
verses.literal: But nothing unclean will ever enter . . . it nor anyone who practices an abomination or a lie but only . . . those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life
verses.literalPt: Nela não entrará coisa alguma impura, nem o que pratica abominação e mentira, mas somente os que estão escritos no livro da vida do Cordeiro.
